denial_rate_note: Structurally near zero and not published. Gov. Code 65850.5(b) makes approval nondiscretionary -- review is 'limited to the building official's review of whether it meets all health and safety requirements' -- so the only denial route is a substantial-evidence finding of specific, adverse impact that forces a use permit. On the SolarAPP+ path the analogue of denial is automated rejection of a non-compliant application (A04), which is a rework loop, not a decision. Neither Oakland nor SolarAPP+ publishes a rejection rate.

timing_gold.end_to_end_scope: permit submission -> final passed inspection, business days, all SolarAPP+ permits, 29 AHJs nationally (2024). This is the only end-to-end figure that isolates the SolarAPP+ path; it stops short of PTO.

timing_gold.source: Performance Review 2024 (S38) for the SolarAPP+ path; SolarTRACE 2025-09-09 dataset (S48b) for Oakland x PG&E phase medians and for the permit-to-PTO total; PG&E Rule 21 tariff and NEM page (S151, S153) for the interconnection commitment.

permit.note: Instant issuance for code-compliant applications; median SolarAPP+ permit review duration = 0 days, versus a 7-day median for traditional permits in the same 33 AHJs. Oakland's own pre-SolarAPP+ baseline was an average of 5-7 days across 2,375 permits in 2022, and the city advertises a 5-day average saving. CONFLICT: SolarTRACE's Oakland-city AHJ-wide median permit time was 9 business days in 2023 and 10 in 2024 for 0-10 kW PV-only, because SolarTRACE pools all permit types at the AHJ level rather than isolating the SolarAPP+ record type (Oakland's 2024 PV+storage figure is 0.0).

inspection.note: Oakland city x PG&E, 0-10 kW PV-only, 2023: install complete -> last passed inspection median 7.0 business days (n=262), down from 20.5 in 2022; PV+storage 7.5. p90 is the national 2023 inspection-phase value; no AHJ-level percentile is published. Oakland's ordinance promises scheduling within 2 business days of a request and exactly one consolidated inspection; SolarTRACE independently records 'Number of Inspections Required' = 1 for Oakland.

known_gaps: No record of Oakland's decision to adopt SolarAPP+ exists. Legistar/Granicus were searched and returned nothing; the 2015 checklist ordinance (Ordinance No. 13332 C.M.S.) has a full staff report and council vote, but the SolarAPP+ rollout appears to have been pure administrative action. A10 and A11 are therefore reconstructed from SolarAPP+'s generic AHJ-registration guide, not from any Oakland document.

The Oakland SolarAPP+ permit fee is not published. Oakland's program page says 'Pay online and receive permit' without an amount, and Sacramento County's page likewise states a SolarAPP+/NREL processing fee exists without quantifying it. The $385 in A08 is SolarTRACE's observed median residential 1-10 kW permit cost for the Oakland AHJ, not an Oakland fee-schedule line; fee error should be scored against it only with that caveat.

SolarTRACE's Oakland timing rows cannot separate SolarAPP+ permits from traditional ones -- its AHJ-level medians pool both. That is why Oakland's SolarTRACE permit median (9 business days in 2023) contradicts the platform-level median of 0. The two sources measure different populations, and no Oakland-specific SolarAPP+-only permit-time figure exists in any source.

2024 SolarTRACE cells for Oakland rest on 14 PV-only installs and 31 PV+storage installs, far below the 2022-2023 volumes; the dataset was completed 2025-09-09 and 2024 coverage is plainly partial. The 2024 column should not be read as a trend.

Oakland's system-size ceiling is stated inconsistently across its own documents: the news release says 'standard residential systems under 15kW DC', SolarAPP+'s eligibility article says <= 38.4 kW, Gov. Code 65850.52 caps the mandate at 38.4 kW AC, and Gov. Code 65850.5's checklist definition caps at 10 kW AC. Which number Oakland's Accela record type actually enforces is not recoverable.

PG&E's residential interconnection back office is invisible. The tariff gives a 30-business-day outer bound and the NEM page a 5-10-day typical range, but nothing documents the internal steps between receipt and PTO. CPUC Decision D.20-09-035 requires quarterly timeline reporting on 19 metrics, yet the CPUC's own page states it 'did not mandate reporting for net energy metering (NEM) systems smaller than 30 kVA' -- exactly the population in this model.

A14's premise -- that an installer can revise an approved design after an inspector has printed the checklist -- is documented only as a SolarAPP+ platform capability. Whether Oakland inspectors actually re-scan the QR code in the field is unknown, and the failure mode it guards against (inspecting against a superseded checklist) would be invisible in every dataset here.

Oakland runs a second, non-SolarAPP+ path for ground-mounted, ballasted, elevated, BIPV and commercial systems, gated on its own self-certification checklist (S41: structural calculations, attachment-point weight, WKS1 referral, Planning Code 17.120.050 noise standards) plus a Green Halo recycling plan. That path is out of scope for this model and is the natural sibling-disentanglement distractor for scoring.
notes: Why this is the gold for Oakland: the SolarAPP+ platform documentation IS the coded process, so the 'designed tier' here is unusually literal -- A03's compliance engine, A05's Approval Document and A15's site-specific checklist are software outputs, not staff behaviours, and help.gosolarapp.org article 110 states plainly that there is no separate approval artifact because 'applicants proceed to paying their fee and printing the building permit.' Three structural points a solver must get right. (1) The permit track and the interconnection track are legally distinct: Gov. Code 65850.52(g) preserves interconnection untouched, and A22 (uploading the finaled permit to PG&E) is the single load-bearing seam -- PG&E's tariff will not start its 30-business-day clock without the AHJ's final electric inspection clearance, so instant permitting cannot by itself deliver a fast PTO. (2) Oakland's 2015 ordinance already encoded most of what SolarAPP+ automates (same-day OTC or 1-3 business days, one consolidated building+fire inspection, 2-business-day inspection scheduling, written correction notice), so the SolarAPP+ delta in Oakland is smaller than the national SolarAPP+-vs-traditional contrast suggests -- the city's own claim is 5 days saved off a 5-7 day baseline. (3) The three staff_only activities (A10 AHJ configuration, A14 checklist-version currency, A25 CEC reporting) all come from documents whose audience is staff, and none has any Oakland-published counterpart. gold_tier is 'designed+observed' because the graph is designed-tier while every timing figure is records-derived (SolarTRACE project-level data, NLR Performance Review AHJ submissions); per-tier scoring should treat the process model as designed-only. Document ids are the corpus source_ids from corpus/realworld/solar_permit/sources.json, so every evidence span is traceable to a fetched file.
quote_verification: All 76 evidence quotes in this file were machine-verified as verbatim substrings of the saved document extractions in corpus/realworld/solar_permit/, after Unicode NFKC normalisation and folding of curly quotes/apostrophes, en/em dashes, non-breaking spaces, ellipses and PDF ligatures (fi/fl/ff), and after collapsing all whitespace (PDF text extractions wrap mid-sentence, so quotes are contiguous in the normalised stream rather than on one line of the .txt). Quotes from the PG&E Rule 21 tariff additionally required stripping the right-margin change bars that pdftotext emits at end of line. Quotes attributed to S48b are cell text read from the SolarTRACE .xlsx (Information sheet variable descriptions) via openpyxl, not from a .txt. Every quote is 40 words or fewer. 0 unverified quotes.
